result.summary: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. (1) patterns/0 and flagged?/1 do not appear in `git diff origin/main..0df7e644` (hunks start at line 42 '@@ -42,11 +42,53 @@' and '@@ -88,32 +130,20 @@'; the three regexes env_assignment/mapping_entry/put_env_literal are untouched context). (2) File set: old = ls-files + regular + size<=4MB + valid UTF-8 + :binary.match. New = `git grep -l -z -F -e LETFLOW_SMTP_` + same filters (Enum.sort only reorders). git grep -l lists binary matches (no -I). Verified read-only: git grep candidates (30) == `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 grep -l -F LETFLOW_SMTP_` (30), diff SAME. Divergence checks on this repo: 0 symlinks (ls-files -s mode 120000: 0; core.symlinks=false), 0 submodules (mode 160000: 0), no sparse-checkout, 0 assume-unchanged/skip-worktree (ls-files -v lowercase/S: 0), no `git config grep.*` keys (only diff.astextplain.textconv), no binary/-diff attrs set on any file (check-attr), -F with ASCII literal is case-sensitive and byte-exact like :binary.match; CRLF working-tree files (w/crlf) still match and line handling is unchanged (split on LF, CR left on line as before). Tracked-but-deleted files: git grep skips, old File.regular? false: same. Theoretical divergence only: a tracked symlink whose target (not its link text) contains the needle would be scanned by old, not by new; none exist and core.symlinks=false on Windows; on Linux CI there are 0 symlinks tracked either. (3) Filter order in the `for` preserved (regular?, stat, size, read, valid?, match); the three non-vacuity asserts (.env.example, deploy/.env.example, config/runtime.exs) and length(files) > 1_000 intact. git grep exit handling: 1 -> [], 0 -> parse, other -> raise (stricter than before, good); tracked_files still `{out,0}` match; stderr_to_stdout dropped so stderr cannot pollute paths. Prefilter sound: all three patterns begin with or contain the literal 'LETFLOW_SMTP_' (names = "LETFLOW_SMTP_" <> ...), so a line lacking it cannot match any pattern. (4) Scope: only this test file changed; adds public scan_tracked/1 (@doc false) for the fixture tests being added, mild but justified by the AC. Moduledoc remains accurate (still describes a scan of the tracked tree via git ls-files; the git grep narrowing is an implementation detail, documented in the defp comment).

issues.description:
Committed source has literal newlines inside string literals instead of the 
 escape: `String.split("<newline>")` (new line ~82) and the assert message `"...variable:<newline>" <> Enum.join(hits, "<newline>")`. Semantically identical to "
" (verified 0 CR bytes in the committed blob), but it is a tool-mangled edit, hard to read, easy to break by editors/autocrlf. Recommend ELIXIR-DEV restore `"
"` escapes. Non-blocking.

Redundant :binary.match(content, @needle) != :nomatch filter retained after git grep narrowing; harmless (keeps old semantics literally). Hit ordering is now sorted-path then line order instead of ls-files order; only affects failure message order.
